summary: Complete contributor map of the primary loopback Studio, its separately gated remote listeners, and Kit's terminal companion. Kit covers composition, discovery, sessions, providers, documentation and capability tools, staged review, and responsive presentation. Folder-derived apps, setup, context menus, and in-app docs define extension points. Infrastructure includes reload, provenance, storage, receipts, and revision-checked HTTP writes. Library owns importing and staging while reporting damaged files without changing them. Workbench owns persistent editors for all eight canonical kinds, split panes, preset links to regex and quick-reply sets, and explicit revision-checked saves. Press owns staged export runs, linked riders, bare single-file delivery, plural zip delivery, and honest unknown-loss reporting. Settings derives Appearance, Models, Connections, Studio, Workbench, Remote access, Updates, and About; Connections manages both directions of MCP. Security distinguishes loopback from opt-in remote boundaries while retaining fail-closed parsing, scripts-as-data, and sanitized marks.

sections.title: Kit terminal shell
sections.summary: Kit is a terminal shell: multiline composer, paste cards, a bounded follow-up queue, draft-preserving history and search, interruptible streaming, and a palette that completes command arguments. Right-click pastes text, alt+V pastes an image drawn as shown-not-sent, and a path written into a message becomes reachable for that file alone, drawn as a link. Native scrolling, foldable replies, copy feedback and a stage watcher keep terminal behavior coherent. Atomic sessions support resume, rewind, fork and export; model settings, doctor, inventory and privacy are command surfaces. /rail keeps a preset's block list beside the conversation: ctrl+B moves the keyboard there, ctrl+shift+arrows resize it, ctrl+shift+D switches density, and < and > thumb through the studio's presets. What is on the rail rides in each turn's ambient context, and Enter stages accumulated edits as one ordinary draft at the same Gate. The tool loop performs bounded reads and replaces model save prose with a revision-checked REVIEW CHANGE gate; a conversion gets REVIEW CROSSING. Its third answer holds a call instead of running or denying it. Applies serialize and Backstage retains lifecycle truth.

sections.title: Hyper-modularity (the build's spine)
sections.summary: UI applications are drop-in folders exporting a HoplightApp manifest and component. Bun discovery skips private underscore folders, bundles apps on demand, puts ordinary apps on the Dock, and keeps catalogOnly tools available through the catalog without a central roster. Apps receive AppContext and may reach engine or filesystem behavior only through its API; the shell owns global navigation, tabs, theme, and status. Visual law comes from one token sheet rather than app-local colors or fixed layout. Bright accents remain marks, borders, and spines; any labeled accent fill uses a generated deep companion with stage-white text. Rose, house accent, deck, and per-piece pairs share tested deepening logic.

sections.title: First-run setup (the wizard)
sections.summary: First run is assembled from drop-in SetupStep folders, each declaring its question, options, settings key, optional widget and stage treatment, and recap language. The wizard derives order, progress, defaults, skipping, stage zones, and final summary from discovery; pure selection and sentence logic is tested separately. Settings are an open record parsed fail-closed per known key and persisted under the studio directory. Missing setupComplete opens the wizard; completion applies theme and house accent and follows the manifest-selected first landing, while later starts choose the lowest-order app. Theme changes use View Transitions when appropriate, retain an immediate reduced-motion fallback, persist server-side, and use localStorage only for pre-paint. Serialized PATCH operations ensure concurrent control changes merge rather than overwrite stale documents.

sections.title: The right-click system
sections.summary: One shared context-menu service grows through registration. Surfaces attach typed targets and data to elements, with the deepest matching element winning and a shell-level target always available. Features register any number of item providers for a target type; each provider contributes a section, an empty result denies by absence, and cleanup receives an unregister function. Shell providers currently cover entity actions such as send, show, open beside, split close, and Workbench removal, plus Dock-app and shell navigation actions. A new feature contributes one provider instead of editing a central switch, preserving room-independent behavior for common entity operations.

sections.title: Apps catalog and documentation
sections.summary: The Dock's Add app control discovers the manifest-marked catalog instead of naming an id, and the catalog derives cards from the running app roster. catalogOnly tools such as CSS Workshop and Help/Docs remain bundled without occupying everyday Dock space. Help/Docs reads the committed corpus through the generated docs index, which can merge frontmatter, semantic page summaries, retrieval topics, and nested section anchors. Navigation separates user workflows and platforms from developer API, architecture, data, format, security, extension, and decision material; ADR filenames remain canonical while titles are reader-friendly. Markdown uses the shared sanitizer, figures and images are restricted to generated or committed docs assets, the right rail follows current headings, and packaged content matches GitHub. External GitHub viewing passes through the leaving gate and URL allowlist.

sections.title: Dev live-reload
sections.summary: Development Studio watches src/ui and broadcasts changes to every open page over the /dev/reload server-sent-event stream. Browser bundles are rebuilt per request, so a save produces fresh code instead of a cached build. Packaged executables serve baked assets, return 404 for the development stream, and let the client become quiet without a separate dependency.

sections.title: The card-type chip
sections.summary: Library summaries derive sourceFormat and sourceVariant from the first non-Hoplight escrow record. Labels come from the live format registry rather than a duplicated UI map: platform-specific adapters show platform and variant, generic Tavern/CC content shows Default, and pieces authored without a source adapter display no chip. The badge therefore describes provenance without inventing one for native drafts.

sections.title: The studio store
sections.summary: Canonical Hoplight JSON is the local database: each entity lives at studioDir/kind/id.json as a portable file. Storage never replaces a different piece at the same id; it creates a numbered sibling, enforcing Keep both at persistence. One inventory pass returns healthy summaries and separate bounded records for safe-id JSON files that fail parsing, canonical schema, kind, or id checks. Damaged files are never modified or quarantined.

sections.title: The receipt
sections.summary: The server renders one plain-language import receipt for both shells, ensuring terminal and visual users receive the same explanation. It uses recognizable platform names, a we-read/we-kept voice, and emits conditional lines only when engine evidence supports embedded books, scripts-as-data, or privileged warnings. Unknown files receive a warm failure message. Receipt rendering adds presentation, not new detection or format logic.

sections.title: Endpoints
sections.summary: The HTTP surface serves the shell, token sheet, boot code, discovered app manifests and bundles, and setup-step modules. Settings supports read, replacement, and validated partial merge. Documentation routes expose the generated index, figures, catalog-declared Markdown, and committed assets. Formats, inspect, export, coverage, and Studio routes remain thin engine and storage boundaries. `/api/studio/inventory` returns healthy entities and bounded damaged-file records from one filesystem scan; `/api/studio/list` remains the healthy-only compatibility read. Editor reads can return the complete entity with its revision, and editor saves atomically compare that revision, returning 409 without overwriting newer data. Bundle saves validate the complete canonical batch before any write, then report genuine storage partials honestly. Host-only `/api/remote/*` routes control tunnel and LAN setup, devices, and approvals; `/api/updates/*` routes read release information and perform version switching.

sections.title: The Library room (the shelves - deep browse)
sections.summary: Library presents first-run doors when empty and, when populated, live per-kind deck counts, a drop-in proscenium view, portrait-backed covers, drop-anywhere import receipts, and the configured initial deck. It loads healthy summaries and damaged records together through one `/api/studio/inventory` filesystem pass and renders an expandable notice even when no readable pieces remain. The notice names each file and bounded reason, states that Hoplight did not change it, includes the local studio path when available, and offers manual restore-or-remove guidance. Grid, showcase, and list are DeckView modules behind the one browser registry seam; each receives consistent open and staged states. Tapping ordinary pieces toggles a staging set that survives deck switches, then sendMany moves the batch through one follow decision reporting the true newly opened count. Already-open pieces remain annotation-only, while the context menu preserves one-shot Send. A continuous, fail-closed 4-to-36rem art-size control updates CSS live and persists on release. View choice and size live in per-user Library preferences.
topics: drop-in grid showcase and list views

sections.title: The Workbench room (home by default - the IDE)
sections.summary: Workbench is the shell-owned tabbed IDE for all eight canonical kinds: character, lorebook, persona, preset, regex, pack, quick-reply set, and HTML document. Editors keep local drafts, load a complete-entity revision, and compare it on explicit save; an external write leaves the draft dirty and reports a conflict. One shared guard owns dirty state, Ctrl+S, close protection, and discard confirmation. Character edits preserve untouched fields and variants through operations shared with Kit. Preset groups render hierarchically, and settings link independently stored regex and quick-reply sets by canonical id. The quick-reply editor manages ordered labels and messages with the same save contract. Split view pairs any two kinds with tested focus and close rules; pane container queries drive collapse. Lorebook editing focuses one searchable entry with triggers, timing, placement, text, platform fields, match tests, and token estimates.

sections.title: The Press room (batch export - the staged set prints)
sections.summary: Press exports only a shell-owned staged queue assembled from Library or its unstaged-piece rail, so queue state survives app switches and the room does not duplicate a studio browser. Linked pieces ride as bundles: characters gather referenced lorebooks, while presets gather behaviorRefs regex sets and quickReplyRefs quick-reply sets, resolved by both kind and id. Riders may be dropped for one run, and already staged riders are not duplicated. Readiness compares characters with the target's live coverage claims and identifies lorebook entries that cannot fire, offering repair links without manufacturing green status when claims are absent. Undeclared coverage remains unknown with a null dropped count. Each run chooses one platform target, declares names and skips before work, and reports each row honestly. One printed file is delivered bare under its own name; several are delivered as one zip. Delivery history, saved jobs, reorder, byte rehearsal, and readiness dots remain deferred.

sections.title: The Agent window (the model, standing on the screen you came from)
sections.summary: A conversation with whatever model the vault holds, carrying the real tool belt. The window owns no provider and no tools: it asks the loopback server, which asks Kit, so there is one vault, one egress ledger and one Gate. The Gate is the layout, not a dialog: a card takes the bottom of the window and the server dispatch loop parks until it is answered. It sees the screen because each app publishes an agentSurface and the mounted app adds what is on it now, joined into a brief that truncates a describe at 300 characters. That snapshot travels through the context both ways, never by importing live-state: every app is bundled separately, so its own import is a second empty copy. The shell publishes a bare snapshot as any app mounts, so apps that never publish still give the window a reading. The studio-change stream reports the folder rather than an actor, so an agent write and a drag from Explorer arrive alike. Replies are drawn from React elements, never from an HTML string.

sections.title: CSS Workshop (catalog-only - assisted CSS authoring)
sections.summary: A catalog-only room for authoring the CSS a card or a host will carry, rather than the CSS this app is built from. It offers starters to begin from, property knobs for the common adjustments, the plain CSS source for anything the knobs do not reach, and a sealed preview showing the result. The output leaves by copy or download for any host, and the room writes no studio state of its own, so nothing here is a piece and nothing needs saving. The preview uses the same seal every untrusted-markup surface in this app uses, which is what lets it show authored CSS without that CSS reaching the application around it.

sections.title: Help / Docs (catalog-only - the corpus, in the app)
sections.summary: The committed documentation corpus presented as a first-class room, read from the same source GitHub serves so the app and the repository can never disagree about what a page says. It reads the generated index at docs/generated/docs-index.json rather than crawling the documentation tree, which has a consequence worth knowing: a page whose semantic sidecar is missing, stale or unapproved stays out of the app exactly as it stays out of CI, because both read that one index. Keeping documentation inside the app means somebody can answer a question without leaving the studio, and means the docs gates protect what users read rather than only what the repository ships.

sections.title: The Macro Lab (catalog-only - what a macro actually does)
sections.summary: A scratch pad for macro text and the only surface that needs no piece open to be useful. It keeps two answers apart on purpose. Reading is pure and local: each token is broken out against the chosen platform catalog, nested tokens report under their container, and where else does it work asks the translator rather than two catalogs, so a shared name meaning different things is a flagged collision instead of a clean trip. A token invoking no name is called that rather than supported, because isMacroSupported fails lenient by design. Resolving runs the text through the platform real engine as a one-block preset behind a host-only route, needs a local checkout pointed at in Settings or named by an environment variable, and refuses by name when absent. The bible lists every macro with click-to-insert, and the operations table derives from the catalogs with gaps sorted first.

sections.title: HTML View (catalog-only - a drawing at full size)
sections.summary: A catalog-only app that draws one htmldoc piece as a whole tab. It is reached three ways: opened by id from the Library, handed a piece by another surface, or handed the raw text of a fenced html block from an agent reply. A piece travels by ID and is re-read from the studio, so the tab shows what the drawing says now; only an unsaved reply is carried whole, and the room says so rather than showing an empty frame. Everything drawn passes through SealedHtmlPreview, the component behind the transcript preview and the Workbench editor pane too, so one boundary serves three sizes with nothing to drift. The tab and the editor pane fill their room while the transcript keeps the inline ceiling, and either goes fullscreen, natively where allowed and as an overlay where not. All CSS renders, head styles included: a document's style blocks are lifted out and re-injected, because sanitizing returns the body alone. JavaScript never runs, no remote image or webfont loads, and form controls are stripped, since the same component draws untrusted card backdrops.

sections.title: Settings (drop-in sections)
sections.summary: Settings tabs derive from section modules exporting id, label, order, and a component that receives AppContext. The section registry is the sole browser seam, so adding configuration does not require a central tab switch. Controls operate against current persisted settings and immediately repaint visual choices. Shipping sections are Appearance, Models, Connections, Studio for home app, initial deck, publish targets and this machine engine checkouts, Workbench, Remote access, Updates, and About. Connections manages MCP both ways: servers this machine runs join Kit belt, added with command, args and write-only env, tested by throwaway spawn, every external tool egress-gated, the whole api mcp surface host-only since an entry is a command this machine executes; and a card shows the one line registering Hoplight own belt in any client. Engine checkouts are similarly machine facts: a root lives in engines.json, travels only over the host-only macro-lab roots route, is normalized and marker-checked before storage, is outranked by an environment variable, and is the file Kit reads at session build.
topics: Studio home deck targets and engine checkouts

sections.title: Shared components (`src/ui/_shared/` and `src/ui/components/`)
sections.summary: Shared visual controls are extracted once for setup, settings, and future editors. SwatchRow exposes the house palette as quick choices and optionally opens PaintPicker for a custom solid color. ColorPicker provides a branded saturation/value square, hue strip, and hex input while retaining HSV internally to avoid grayscale-state loss. Pure color math normalizes and converts values fail-closed and shares pointer fractions across color and gradient controls. The Paint model is a validated discriminated union for solid, linear, and radial output; gradients require at least two valid stops. PaintPicker composes color editing, stop add/drag/remove, angle adjustment, and curved previews behind allowed-mode gates. Solid accent use is live; tested gradient editing awaits its first entity or pack background consumer.

sections.title: Security
sections.summary: The primary Studio listener binds loopback. Optional remote listeners are separate, explicitly enabled boundaries with join secrets, device approval, and host-only controls. Uploads use the CLI engine's fail-closed format parsers and archive-expansion limits rather than a permissive UI parser. Scripts stored inside entities remain data throughout Studio workflows. Third-party manifest SVG marks are sanitized before Dock or catalog insertion, removing scripts, foreignObject content, and event handlers.
